content:
Google today announced that NotebookLM is being renamed "Gemini Notebook" starting today, and previewed upcoming new features for users.

Unveiled as Project Tailwind at the 2023 I/O conference, the research tool was later renamed NotebookLM shortly before its official launch. Compared to retaining the term "language model" in the name, Gemini Notebook sounds more approachable, while clearly tying the app to Google's Gemini brand.

The existing logo will be replaced with a blue-to-purple gradient Gemini logo design.

Gemini Notebook remains "a standalone product focused on being your go-to research tool," but will in the future "play a greater role within the Google ecosystem".

Notebook features are already available within the Gemini app, allowing users to organise conversations and gather information; this feature will also soon arrive in Google's AI Mode in Search.

Another announcement today is that the upgraded versions of Gemini 3.5 and Antigravity, which were first rolled out to AI Ultra subscribers in December last year, will soon be available to AI Pro subscribers. Every Notebook comes with a secure cloud computer that can natively write and execute code to support "complex data analysis based on sources". Google emphasised that "new output formats and deeper analysis" will be introduced.

This upgrade will be available to all Google AI Pro users on the web "within the coming weeks".

Google also announced today that Gemini Notebook now has over 30 million users, with more than 600,000 organisational users.
